key_insight: Introduce "epiplexity", a notion of information that measures the amount of useful, learnable content under computational constraints — showing that deterministic transformations can create new, task-relevant information for bounded learners even when classical measures (Shannon/Kolmogorov) say nothing new.
problem_solved: Classical information measures assume unbounded observers and therefore fail to quantify the information that real, computationally-bounded learners can extract or construct from data; this paper provides a framework to evaluate and reason about learnable information independent of specific downstream tasks.
method: Formalize epiplexity as an information measure conditioned on computational budgets and learning procedures, aligning information with what bounded algorithms can feasibly extract.
Prove theoretical properties (e.g., invariances, bounds, composition rules) contrasting epiplexity with Shannon entropy and Kolmogorov complexity.
Empirically demonstrate that deterministic transforms and representation choices can increase epiplexity and reduce sample complexity for realistic learners.
impact: Provides practitioners a principled way to evaluate data, augmentations, and representations for real-world models with limited compute — guiding dataset design, augmentation strategies, and model selection toward information that is actually learnable.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: Shannon entropy vs epiplexity — show same data entropy but different epiplexity under computational constraints.
Flow diagram: deterministic transform applied to raw data → increased epiplexity → improved learner performance (fewer samples).
Plot: sample complexity or test accuracy vs epiplexity, demonstrating correlation between higher epiplexity and faster learning.
Icon set: compute budget (clock/CPU), data (stacked cards), and learnable signal (magnifying glass) to emphasize bounded observers.
paper_title: From Entropy to Epiplexity: Rethinking Information for Computationally Bounded Intelligence
paper_authors: Marc Finzi, Shikai Qiu, Yiding Jiang, Pavel Izmailov, J. Zico Kolter
